items.title: Short-term Efficacy of massage and related treatments for Ankylosing Spondylitis: A Systematic Review and Meta Analysis.
items.abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease causing significant pain, stiffness, and functional impairment. Conventional treatments are limited by adverse events and poor efficacy for axial manifestations, leading AS patients to seek complementary therapies such as massage. However, no systematic reviews or meta-analyses have synthesized evidence on massage for AS, leaving its efficacy unconfirmed. From inception to July 5, 2025, a comprehensive literature search was conducted using eight electronic databases to identify randomized controlled trials of massage and related treatments for AS. Risk of bias was assessed via Cochrane RoB 2, and data was synthesized using Review Manager 5.4. Subgroup analysis was performed according to the different intervention methods. The I2 statistic was used to assess the heterogeneity. Seventeen RCTs involving 1,687 patients were included. Meta-analysis demonstrated that massage significantly improved disease activity (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index [BASDAI]: SMD = -1.09, 95% CI: -1.38 to -0.80, P < 0.001), physical function (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index [BASFI]: SMD = -1.00, 95% CI: -1.33 to -0.67, P < 0.001), spinal pain (Visual Analog Scale [VAS-pain]: MD = -1.43, 95% CI: -1.80 to -1.05, P < 0.001), and inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate [ESR]: MD = -3.58, 95% CI: -4.71 to -2.99, P < 0.001; C-reactive protein [CRP]: SMD = -0.73, 95% CI: -1.03 to -0.43, P < 0.001) compared to control groups. Subgroup analysis suggested that massage alone might be more effective than massage combined with other therapies like acupuncture. Significant heterogeneity was observed, attributable to variations in massage techniques and protocols. Of note, the long-term efficacy of massage was not evaluated in this review, as no included studies provided follow‑up beyond the treatment period. Massage and related treatments are effective in alleviating disease activity, improving physical function, reducing pain, and lowering inflammation in patients with ankylosing spondylitis. It can be considered as a beneficial non-pharmacological adjunct for AS. However, these findings must be interpreted with caution due to several limitations inherent in the included studies, including methodological flaws, small sample sizes, inconsistent treatment protocols, and insufficient statistical precision. Moreover, blinding was not feasible in massage therapy, which precludes exclusion of potential placebo or observer effects. Therefore, future high‑quality, standardized, and longitudinal RCTs are warranted to confirm the role of massage in evidence‑based AS management.

items.title: Isolated Bilateral Periocular Lupus Miliaris Disseminatus Faciei: A Clinicopathological Mimicker of Granulomatosis With Polyangiitis.
items.abstract: BACKGROUND Lupus miliaris disseminatus faciei (LMDF) is a rare idiopathic granulomatous dermatosis that presents as discrete yellow-brown, erythematous, or skin-colored papules on the central face, with a recognized preference for the eyelids and periorbital region. CASE REPORT We report a case of isolated bilateral periocular LMDF in a healthy young adult man whose initial eyelid biopsy revealed suppurative necrotizing granulomatous inflammation, raising histopathological concern for granulomatosis with polyangiitis and other systemic granulomatous diseases. Autoimmune, vasculitic, infectious, urinary, orbital, and thoracic evaluations were otherwise negative, apart from only mild inflammatory marker elevation, with an erythrocyte sedimentation rate of 21 mm/h (reference range, 0-20 mm/h) and C-reactive protein level of 0.94 mg/dL (reference range, 0.1-0.5 mg/dL). The final diagnosis was supported by the clinicopathological combination of symmetrical folliculocentric periocular papules, perifollicular necrobiotic suppurative granulomas, absence of true vasculitis, negative infectious studies, and absence of systemic disease. After 1 month of extended-release oral minocycline, the patient had marked flattening of papules and near-complete resolution of crusted inflammatory lesions. Adverse effects were monitored clinically during routine follow-up after completion of the 1-month treatment course; the patient reported no treatment-related adverse effects, and no adverse effects were observed. CONCLUSIONS Clinicopathological correlation and comprehensive systemic evaluation are necessary to differentiate this rare dermatosis from infectious or vasculitic mimics. In this patient, oral minocycline was associated with marked short-term clinical improvement after 1 month, but this single observation does not establish broader therapeutic efficacy for LMDF.

items.title: Early renal response and baseline serum albumin in childhood proliferative lupus nephritis managed with a mycophenolate mofetil-first, response-guided strategy.
items.abstract: Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) is a recommended first-line treatment option for proliferative lupus nephritis (LN), but evidence from pediatric real-world cohorts remains limited. We evaluated short-term renal response and baseline factors associated with time to first complete renal response (CRR) in Vietnamese children managed with an MMF-first, response-guided strategy. We retrospectively studied children aged ≤16 years with biopsy-proven proliferative LN selected for an institutional MMF-first, response-guided strategy. The primary outcome was time to first CRR within 6 months. Kaplan-Meier and Cox analyses were performed; baseline serum albumin was modeled with a time-varying coefficient because the proportional hazards assumption was not met. Among 66 children, 61 (92.4%) achieved a first CRR within 6 months (median, 3 months), and 56 (84.8%) were in CRR at month 6. Higher baseline serum albumin was associated with earlier first CRR after adjustment for baseline proteinuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate, although this association attenuated over time (time-varying effect, P = 0.008). In exploratory analyses, children with baseline serum albumin ≤2.5 g/dL achieved first CRR later than those with higher albumin. Children selected for an MMF-first, response-guided strategy had favorable short-term renal response. Higher baseline serum albumin was associated with earlier CRR, particularly during the early treatment period, but should be interpreted as a marker of response kinetics rather than a validated independent predictor. These findings should not be generalized to children with severe proliferative LN requiring an alternative initial treatment strategy.

items.title: Therapeutic Drug Monitoring of Golimumab to Predict Disease Activity and Antidrug Antibodies Status in Patients with Ankylosing Spondylitis.
items.abstract: Golimumab is a fully human tumor necrosis factor-alpha inhibitor that is highly effective in the management of ankylosing spondylitis (AS). A major limitation of golimumab is nonresponse, resulting from low drug concentrations, which is primarily due to antidrug antibodies (ADAs). The aim of this study was to assess the trough concentration of golimumab and the prevalence of ADA formation in patients with AS. An enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay was used to quantify golimumab trough concentrations and ADAs in 59 Iraqi patients with AS; AS disease activity was also evaluated using the Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Score (ASDAS). Regression analysis was performed to determine predictors of disease activity and ADA formation. The mean age of the participants was 37.86 years, most of them (52 patients) were men, and the median number of golimumab doses administered was 7. The median ASDAS score was 3.1, and approximately 35% of patients had low disease activity (ASDAS score <2.1). The range of golimumab trough concentration was 0.21-1.38 mg/L with a median of 0.41 mg/L, and ADAs were detected in 8 patients (13.6%). Trough concentrations were higher in ADA-negative patients and were significantly negatively correlated with ASDAS scores. Regression analysis identified the trough drug concentration as the only predictor of both disease activity and ADA formation, with lower concentrations responsible for higher disease activity and a higher chance of developing ADAs. Drug concentration is an important determinant of disease activity, and routine monitoring of trough concentration is recommended for therapeutic drug monitoring of golimumab.

items.title: Health literacy among people with systemic sclerosis: a scleroderma patient-centred intervention network (SPIN) cohort cross-sectional study.
items.abstract: Health literacy reflects the ability to find, understand, evaluate, and use information to make health-related decisions. We evaluated sociodemographic and disease factors associated with health literacy among people with systemic sclerosis (SSc). Participants with SSc in the Scleroderma Patient-centred Intervention Network Cohort completed the Health Literacy Scale19-12 Item Questionnaire from February to November 2025. Multivariable linear regression was used to assess associations of sociodemographic and disease characteristics with health literacy. The 1,019 participants were mainly female (N = 898, 88%) and White (N = 850, 84%). Mean (SD) years of education was 15.5 (3.9). Most had limited cutaneous SSc (N = 669, 66%). Mean health literacy total score was 69.7; 438 (43%) participants had excellent or sufficient and 581 (57%) had problematic or inadequate health literacy. Education (1.63 points per 5 years, 95% CI 0.25 to 3.01) was significantly associated with higher health literacy scores. Compared to the United States, participants from Canada (-4.98 points, 95% CI -7.99 to -1.97), the United Kingdom (-7.79 points, 95% CI -12.03 to -3.55), France (-6.05 points, 95% CI -8.84 to -3.27), and Australia, Mexico, or Spain (-7.02 points, 95% CI -12.39 to -1.66) had significantly lower health literacy scores. Age, gender, race or ethnicity, marital status, time since first non-Raynaud symptom onset, and disease subtype were not associated with health literacy. The association between health literacy and education was small. Differences between countries may reflect self-evaluation tendencies. More work is needed to better understand health literacy measurement.

items.title: Clinical and Immunological Associations of Anti-Ro52 Antibody Positivity in Primary Sjögren Disease: A Retrospective Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: To characterize the clinical and immunological correlates of anti-Ro52/TRIM21 antibody positivity in primary Sjögren disease (pSjD), focusing on prevalent interstitial lung disease (ILD), hematological abnormalities, and peripheral immune features. This single-center retrospective cross-sectional study included 122 adults fulfilling the 2016 ACR/EULAR classification criteria (81 anti-Ro52-positive; 41 anti-Ro52-negative). Prespecified outcomes were prevalent ILD and hematological abnormalities. Anti-Ro52/anti-Ro60 profiles, lymphocyte subsets, absolute lymphocyte counts, and 12 circulating cytokines were assessed. Multiple immune comparisons were controlled using Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Firth penalized logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, disease duration, and anti-Ro60 status; modified Poisson models estimated adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs). ILD occurred in 19/81 (23.5%) anti-Ro52-positive and 3/41 (7.3%) anti-Ro52-negative patients (P=0.044); hematological abnormalities occurred in 16/81 (19.8%) and 2/41 (4.9%), respectively (P=0.032). In adjusted Firth models, anti-Ro52 positivity was not statistically associated with ILD (OR 2.95, 95% CI 0.91-12.26; P=0.074), whereas the association with hematological abnormalities remained evident (OR 5.05, 95% CI 1.28-30.44; P=0.018). Modified Poisson estimates were directionally similar. Anti-Ro52-positive patients had higher CD19+ B-cell percentages and lower natural killer-cell percentages; both remained significant after FDR correction. Absolute B-cell counts did not differ, whereas absolute natural killer-cell counts were lower. No cytokine remained significant after FDR correction. Anti-Ro52 positivity was associated with distinct clinical and peripheral immune features in hospitalized patients with pSjD. The ILD association was attenuated after adjustment for anti-Ro60 and demographic factors, whereas the hematological association remained statistically evident but imprecise. These findings support interpretation of anti-Ro52 within a broader serological and immunological context.

items.title: From immune heterogeneity to targeted therapies in IgG4-related disease.
items.abstract: Recent advances in single-cell, spatial, and multiomic technologies have provided new insights into the immunopathogenesis and clinical heterogeneity of IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD). At the same time, several mechanism-based therapies have entered clinical development. Recent studies have identified distinct B-cell, T-cell, myeloid, and stromal populations and their interactions within affected tissues. Type 2 peripheral helper T-cell-associated, granzyme K+ cytotoxic T-cell-associated, and age-associated B-cell-related programs may contribute to tissue inflammation and immune dysregulation. Recent studies further suggest that immunopathogenesis varies across clinical phenotypes and may be shaped by additional axes such as allergy and malignancy. Clinical trials have demonstrated efficacy of the CD19-directed B-cell-depleting therapy with inebilizumab and the nondepleting B-cell modulator obexelimab, while Bruton tyrosin kinase inhibition and cellular therapies represent emerging therapeutic approaches. IgG4-RD is increasingly recognized as an immunologically heterogeneous fibroinflammatory disease. Integrating immune pathotypes with clinical phenotypes and dynamic biomarkers may enable more individualized treatment and accelerate development of mechanism-based therapies.

items.title: Reduction in Rheumatoid Factor and Matrix Metalloproteinase-3 With Successful Glucocorticoid Withdrawal After Initiation of Pemafibrate in a Patient With Rheumatoid Arthritis and Hypertriglyceridemia: A Case Report.
items.abstract: Pemafibrate is a selective peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα) modulator (SPPARMα) used for hypertriglyceridemia. PPARα activation also suppresses nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling, a pathway central to synovial inflammation and joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Whether pemafibrate affects RA-related biomarkers in humans is unknown. A 51-year-old woman (height: 164 cm, body weight: 71 kg, body mass index: 26.4 kg/m²) with RA treated with methotrexate, bucillamine, iguratimod, and low-dose prednisolone (0.7 mg/day) had hypertriglyceridemia with coexisting metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Pemafibrate was started at 0.2 mg/day and increased to 0.4 mg/day after 12 weeks, while the disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) regimen was kept unchanged throughout. Over the 20 months following the initiation of pemafibrate, rheumatoid factor (RF) and matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) declined, and C-reactive protein (CRP) showed an overall decrease with a transient rise at month 6; prednisolone was tapered and discontinued after 17 months. The 28-joint Disease Activity Score based on C-reactive protein (CRP; DAS28-CRP), already in the remission range at baseline (1.9), remained below the remission threshold throughout. Serum triglycerides fell from 184 mg/dL to 88 mg/dL, and hepatic transaminases (aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT)) showed a transient early increase followed by a return toward baseline, without meeting criteria for drug-induced liver injury. No adverse events attributable to pemafibrate were observed. In this patient, the introduction of pemafibrate was temporally associated with reductions in RA-related biomarkers and with successful glucocorticoid withdrawal, without any intensification of DMARD therapy. Because the baseline prednisolone dose was already low (0.7 mg/day), this withdrawal should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as strong evidence of a glucocorticoid-sparing effect. Causality cannot be established from a single case; nevertheless, together with earlier clinical reports on fenofibrate, animal studies showing anti-arthritic effects of fenofibrate and bezafibrate, and preclinical evidence of PPARα-mediated NF-κB inhibition, this observation suggests that PPARα agonists merit further investigation as adjunctive agents in RA, particularly in patients with coexisting dyslipidemia or steatotic liver disease.

items.title: Cystic pulmonary amyloidosis with lymphoid interstitial pneumonia in Sjögren's disease: a case report.
items.abstract: Interstitial lung diseases are commonly seen in association with Sjögren's disease, especially lymphoproliferative disorders, such as lymphoid interstitial pneumonia. In occasional and rare cases, pulmonary amyloidosis with cysts, nodules, and/or ground-glass opacites as radiological features, can also become a complication of Sjögren's disease. On the other hand, diffuse cystic lung disease, without nodules, concomitant with chylous fluid accumulation in female leads to initial suspicion of lymphangioleiomyomatosis. Interestingly, it's challenging to differentiate if diffuse cystic lung lesion absent of nodules, chylous fluid accumulation and Sjögren's disease happen simultaneously. A 34-year-old female, with diffuse cystic lung disease, chylous reflux lymphedema and Sjögren's disease, was eventually diagnosed with cystic pulmonary amyloidosis with lymphoid interstitial pneumonia, secondary to Sjögren's disease, and chylous reflux lymphedema as comorbidity. The case presented with atypical pulmonary amyloidosis radiological features of lung lesion, where diffuse cysts existed without nodules or ground-glass opacites, apart from the scarcely seen size of the biggest cyst. The patient was diagnosed with CPA with LIP, secondary to SjD. Clinical symptoms were relieved after thoracoscopic lobectomy of the right lower lobe, where located the biggest cyst. The immunosuppressants that she had been taking were recommended again for disease stabilization. Cystic pulmonary amyloidosis is a rare complication of Sjögren's disease, while lymphoid interstitial pneumonia is comparatively well-known. There can be cystic pulmonary amyloidosis cases where the lung lesion only consists of diffuse, thin-walled, and variably-sized cysts, with the absence of nodules or ground-glass opacities, which warrants a lung biopsy. Clinicians should be alerted to the cyst-only radiological features of the cystic pulmonary amyloidosis with Sjögren's disease.

items.title: Beyond thrombosis: a scoping review of patient-reported outcomes in antiphospholipid syndrome.
items.abstract: Antiphospholipid syndrome (APS) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by thrombosis and pregnancy morbidity, with heterogeneous nonthrombotic manifestations that may substantially affect daily functioning and well-being. Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) offer a direct assessment of symptom burden and quality of life but remain underutilized in APS. We performed a scoping review of PubMed from inception through July 2025 using terms related to APS and PROs (quality of life, fatigue, pain, depression, psychological well-being, and health surveys). We included eligible English-language studies that reported PROs in APS. Both qualitative and quantitative studies were included. Twelve cohort studies evaluated PROs in APS. Most studies used legacy instruments such as the 36-item short form health survey. A few recent studies have used patient-reported outcomes measurement information system (PROMIS) tools. Across studies, patients with APS reported impairments in multiple domains of health-related quality of life (HRQOL) as well as overall HRQOL compared with population norms, which are associated with comorbid systemic lupus erythematosus (secondary APS), a history of thrombosis, and greater end-organ damage. Anticoagulation monitoring and international normalized ratio lability contributed to treatment dissatisfaction and reduced HRQOL. Major gaps include the longitudinal assessment of PROs and their temporal relation to clinical events and the evaluation of PROs in obstetric APS and children and older adults with APS. No APS-specific PRO instruments have been developed. There is a need to either develop APS-specific instruments or validate generic instruments such as PROMIS measures in large representative APS cohorts. Incorporating PROs into clinical practice and research can enhance clinical care and facilitate patient-centered, personalized management of APS.

items.title: Hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness in patients with gout: a controlled cross-sectional elastography study.
items.abstract: Gout shares cardiometabolic risk factors with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). We aimed to compare elastography-defined hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness between patients with gout and metabolically stringent controls, and to identify independent determinants of controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM). In this single-center cross-sectional study (April 2024-January 2026), 201 adults with gout and 80 controls free of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease underwent vibration-controlled transient elastography (FibroScan®). Multivariable linear and logistic regression models identified independent predictors of CAP, LSM, and binary elastographic outcomes. Patients with gout had significantly higher CAP (279 vs. 251.5 dB/m; p < 0.001) and LSM (6.1 vs. 5.1 kPa; p < 0.001). In unadjusted analyses, the odds of hepatic steatosis (CAP ≥ 238 dB/m; OR 2.42, 95% CI 1.40-4.20; p = 0.001) and of increased liver stiffness (LSM ≥ 7.0 kPa; OR 2.46, 95% CI 1.27-4.78; p = 0.007) were higher in the gout group, and LSM ≥ 9.6 kPa was more frequent (12.9% vs. 1.3%; p = 0.001). On multivariable analysis, BMI and ALT were the principal determinants of CAP, whereas BMI and age independently predicted continuous LSM. Gout status was not independently associated with CAP, continuous LSM, hepatic steatosis, or increased liver stiffness (adjusted OR 1.83, 95% CI 0.84-4.01; p = 0.131). Serum uric acid and disease activity measures were not associated with any elastographic outcome. Patients with gout exhibit a substantially higher burden of elastography-defined hepatic steatosis and increased liver stiffness than metabolically stringent controls. This excess was accounted for by adiposity and age rather than by gout status or urate levels, suggesting that non-invasive liver assessment in gout should be guided by cardiometabolic risk profile rather than by the diagnosis of gout itself. Key Points • In unadjusted analyses, patients with gout had more than twofold higher odds of both hepatic steatosis and increased liver stiffness on transient elastography compared with metabolically stringent controls. • BMI and ALT were the strongest independent determinants of CAP; BMI and age were the strongest determinants of continuous LSM. • After adjustment for age, BMI and cardiometabolic covariates, gout status was not independently associated with any elastographic outcome, including increased liver stiffness (LSM ≥ 7.0 kPa). • Serum uric acid, disease activity scores, and urate-lowering or anti-inflammatory therapies were not associated with elastographic liver measures, indicating that hepatic involvement in gout reflects adiposity-driven metabolic burden rather than urate-specific mechanisms.

items.title: Emerging therapeutic role of cinnamic acid derivatives in hyperuricemia and gout: mechanistic, translational, and pharmacological perspectives.
items.abstract: Hyperuricemia and gout are increasingly common metabolic and inflammatory disorders characterized by excessive accumulation of uric acid, impaired urate excretion, oxidative stress, and monosodium urate crystal inflammation. Although currently available therapies such as xanthine oxidase inhibitors and uricosuric agents effectively reduce serum levels of uric acid, their long-term clinical use is often associated with adverse reactions, limited tolerability, and incomplete disease management. As a result, there is increasing interest in identifying natural compounds that may serve as a potential preclinical lead for the development of more targeted urate-lowering strategies. Cinnamic acid derivatives, including p-coumaric acid, caffeic acid, ferulic acid, sinapic acid, chlorogenic acid, and synthetic analogs such as 4-nitrocinnamic acid, have shown promising anti-hyperuricemic and anti-gout activities in experimental studies. These compounds have pharmacological effects through several mechanisms, including the inhibition of xanthine oxidase; modulation of urate transporters such as URAT1, GLUT9, and ABCG2; suppression of inflammatory pathways including NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome signalling; antioxidant activity; and protection against renal injuries induced by uric acid. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms, pharmacological evidence, and structure-activity relationships of selected cinnamic acid derivatives related to hyperuricemia and gout management. In addition, it discusses translational challenges associated with bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, toxicity evaluation, and clinical validation. Collectively, cinnamic acid derivatives represent promising pre-clinical leads that warrant further preclinical and clinical investigations to develop safer and more effective therapies against hyperuricemia and gout.

items.title: Real-world Evidence of Anifrolumab Use in Mexican Patients With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Multicenter Observational Study.
items.abstract: Anifrolumab is a monoclonal antibody directed against type I interferon receptor subunit 1 (IFNAR1) that blocks the interferon signaling pathway associated with key inflammatory processes involved in the pathogenesis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Its specific use in the Mexican population has not been previously evaluated; therefore, this study aimed to assess the impact of anifrolumab therapy on corticosteroid use in Mexican patients with moderate-to-severe SLE. A multicenter, observational medical record review study was conducted from September 2024 to May 2025, including Mexican patients with moderate-to-severe SLE who received anifrolumab for 6 months. The primary outcomes were disease control and remission, as defined by the LLDAS and DORIS criteria, respectively. Secondary outcomes included changes in prednisone use and immunologic (anti-dsDNA and complement levels C3 and C4) and hematological parameters. Seventeen patients were included in the study. At the start of treatment, the average prednisone dose was 23.0±18.0 mg, which was significantly reduced by the third month to 5.0±3.0 mg (p=0.001) and further reduced to 2.5±2.5 mg (p<0.001) by the 6th month. Approximately 41% of patients stopped using prednisone by month 6 of treatment. A total of 62.5% of patients achieved LLDAS by the 3rd month (p=0.008), while 43.8% reached clinical remission through DORIS criteria (p=0.023), and 37.5% reached complete remission (p=0.041) by the 6th month of treatment. Treatment with anifrolumab for 6 months significantly reduced SLE activity, improved immunologic parameters, and reduced corticosteroid use, as reflected by the achievement of therapeutic goals such as LLDAS and DORIS.

items.title: How relationships with exercise change: A qualitative study on the influences of exercise decision-making with systemic lupus erythematosus and cardiovascular disease.
items.abstract: Background: Greater than 50% of individuals with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) will develop cardiovascular disease (CVD). Moderate-intensity aerobic exercise significantly reduces CVD risk, morbidity, and mortality, yet most persons with SLE do not meet the minimum recommendations for physical activity. Purpose: To explore specific barriers to exercise that afflict those with both SLE and CVD, as well as how these factors may change over time. Research Design: Qualitative. Study Sample: Individuals with self-reported SLE and CVD. Data Collection: Researchers conducted 1:1 semi-structured interviews and administered a battery of surveys. Analysis. Researchers used an inductive, interpretive phenomenological analysis qualitative approach to understand patients' perspectives on what influences perception and decision-making of exercise. Results: Five participants completed the study. Four overarching themes were identified. The first, "Short-term Risks versus Long-term Benefits of Exercise," exemplifies the temporal nature of the perception of exercise risk throughout the diagnostic timeline and explains how this relationship changes over time. The second, "Pacing," defines the struggle that these participants face when allocating energy to everyday tasks. The third, "Foundational and Nurturing Supports for Exercise," describes the impact that medical and family/friends have on exercise adherence as primary methods of support. The fourth highlights a "Need for Tailored Intervention" for each patient with SLE and CVD, as general recommendations from health professionals are often described as difficult to adhere to. Conclusion: Understanding exercise adherence in this population represents a dynamic and individualized process. The success of long-term decisions to engage in exercise may result from targeting natural intervention areas across the diagnostic timeline, encouraging support from healthcare providers, friends, and family members, and implementing personalized exercise programs for this population.

items.title: The "living well with lupus" lifestyle intervention: Effects on gut microbiota in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus and high cardiovascular risk.
items.abstract: BackgroundSystemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease associated with increased cardiovascular risk and gut microbiota dysbiosis. Although lifestyle can modulate the microbiome, the impact of multidisciplinary interventions in SLE remains unclear. Thus, the aim of the present study was to investigate the effects of a multidisciplinary lifestyle intervention on gut microbiota diversity and composition in women with SLE and high cardiovascular risk.Materials and methodsThis study analyzed a subsample ( n = 31) from the "Living Well with Lupus" (LWWL) study, a 6-month randomized controlled trial. Patients were assigned to a lifestyle intervention + standard care (LWWL) or a standard care control group (CG). Gut microbiota (16S rRNA sequencing), fecal short-chainfatty acids (SCFAs), selected cardiovascular risk factors, dietary intake, and physical activity levels were assessed before and after the intervention.ResultsNo significant changes were observed in cardiovascular risk factors, food intake, or physical activity levels. Fecal SCFA concentrations and alpha/beta diversity also remained stable. Exploratory taxonomic analyses nevertheless identified distinct relative-abundance patterns across groups and time, including a numerical increase in the Firmicutes -to- Bacteroidota (F/B) ratio in LWWL and different trajectories of several SCFA-associated genera. Among these, Blautia and Parasutterella increased, whereas Butyricimonas , Coprococcus , and Odoribacter decreased from pre- to post-intervention in LWWL, with different trajectories observed in CG across these genera.ConclusionsThese findings suggest that taxonomic features of the gut microbiota may show compositional variation following a lifestyle intervention even in the absence of detectable changes in the measured cardiometabolic or behavioral outcomes. However, the functional and clinical significance of these exploratory taxonomic patterns remains uncertain and warrants further investigation.

items.title: Diagnostic Complexity of Adult-Onset Still's Disease in the Setting of Nosocomial Infection and Antibiotic Hypersensitivity.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still's disease (AOSD) is a diagnosis of exclusion and may be difficult to recognize when infection and drug hypersensitivity coexist. A 31-year-old woman presented with high-spiking fever, arthralgia, and a generalized eruption after ampicillin exposure. Initial investigations for infection and autoimmune disease were unrevealing. Her clinical course was subsequently complicated by severe nosocomial infection and recurrent eruptions during antibiotic treatment. Recurrent high-spiking fever and a fever-associated eruption after apparent clinical improvement of infection supported AOSD as the working diagnosis. However, uncertainty regarding the rash and overlapping infectious and drug-related features limited confident retrospective confirmation of the Yamaguchi classification criteria. Following infection control, intravenous methylprednisolone pulse therapy followed by cyclosporine resulted in rapid clinical improvement. This case illustrates the diagnostic complexity of AOSD in the setting of nosocomial infection and antibiotic hypersensitivity.

items.title: Alpha-ketoglutarate ameliorates systemic sclerosis-associated fibrosis by restoring endothelial function.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a devastating autoimmune disease characterized by multi-organ fibrosis with limited therapeutic options. Using targeted metabolomics, we first observed that levels of alpha-ketoglutarate (α-KG), a key TCA-cycle intermediate, were paradoxically elevated in bleomycin-induced fibrotic lungs and in TGF-β-stimulated fibroblasts, prompting us to test whether exogenous supplementation could augment this compensatory response. Using bleomycin-induced skin and lung fibrosis mouse models, we demonstrated that oral α-KG administration significantly attenuated dermal and pulmonary collagen deposition, reduced inflammatory infiltration, and improved survival. Although fibroblasts are conventionally regarded as the central effectors of fibrosis, integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk transcriptomic deconvolution unexpectedly identified endothelial cells as the predominant cellular target of α-KG in fibrotic lungs. Consistently, α-KG restored endothelial cell proportions in vivo, rescued angiogenic function and preserved barrier integrity in association with upregulation of eNOS, and tight junction proteins in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) treated with bleomycin. Mechanistically, α-KG suppressed TGF-β/Smad activation and reversed bleomycin-induced metabolic repression, including restoration of fatty acid oxidation signatures and mitochondrial ultrastructure, accompanied by upregulation of the mitochondrial biogenesis regulator NRF1. Collectively, these findings reveal that α-KG exerts broad anti-fibrotic effects in SSc models by protecting endothelial function and inhibiting canonical pro-fibrotic signaling, highlighting its potential as a translatable metabolic therapeutic strategy for SSc.

items.title: Circulating miR-21-5p and miR-223-3p as diagnostic biomarkers for rheumatoid arthritis in a sub-Saharan African cohort: a hospital-based case-control study.
items.abstract: Diagnosing rheumatoid arthritis (RA) remains challenging, particularly in resource-constrained settings. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) have emerged as candidate non-invasive biomarkers; however, their expression in African populations has not been systematically evaluated. This hospital-based study drew on a parent cohort of 170 participants (85 patients with rheumatoid arthritis and 85 healthy controls) recruited at Kenyatta National Hospital, Kenya. Circulating miRNAs were quantified in a subsample of 40 participants (20 RA, 20 controls). Two miRNAs (miR-21-5p and miR-223-3p) were measured in plasma using stem-loop RT-qPCR with miR-16-5p as the endogenous control. Relative expression was assessed using the comparative cycle threshold (ΔΔCt) method. Diagnostic performance was evaluated by receiver operating characteristic analysis with bootstrap confidence intervals and bootstrap internal validation, and all comparisons were additionally adjusted for age and sex. Both miRNAs were significantly downregulated in RA patients relative to controls (miR-21-5p fold change 0.21; miR-223-3p fold change 0.35; both P < 0.001), and both differences persisted after adjustment for age and sex (miR-21-5p adjusted P = 0.006; miR-223-3p adjusted P = 0.019). miR-21-5p showed the stronger individual discrimination (AUC 0.900, 95% CI 0.772-0.990) compared with miR-223-3p (AUC 0.857, 95% CI 0.717-0.960). A two-miRNA logistic model achieved an apparent AUC of 0.925 (95% CI 0.820-0.997), corresponding to an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.911 after bootstrap internal validation; this did not significantly exceed miR-21-5p alone (ΔAUC 0.025, P = 0.299). No statistically significant difference was detected between the two-miRNA model and CRP, ACPA or RF, although the study was not powered for equivalence testing. Within RA patients, no correlation between miRNA expression and clinical variables survived correction for multiple testing. Circulating miR-21-5p and miR-223-3p are markedly downregulated in Kenyan patients with rheumatoid arthritis, and miR-21-5p discriminated patients from healthy controls with an apparent AUC of 0.900 (95% CI 0.772-0.990); the two-miRNA logistic model had an apparent AUC of 0.925 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.911. Within-group analyses suggest that age alone is unlikely to account for the between-group difference in miR-21-5p (age explained approximately 1% of the observed difference), although age and disease status are strongly collinear and the age distributions overlap very little. These findings identify circulating miR-21-5p as a credible candidate diagnostic biomarker in a sub-Saharan African population, in which no such evaluation has previously been reported. Consistent with the accepted sequence of biomarker development, establishing clinical diagnostic accuracy now requires validation against early disease and clinically relevant disease controls.

items.title: 5.0-T magnetic resonance imaging and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance angiography for the evaluation of juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
items.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is the most sensitive non-invasive method for assessing joint lesions in juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA), but conventional protocols cannot simultaneously depict synovial inflammation and the associated vascular changes. To assess changes in the "synovium-vascular axis" of the hand in children with JIA using 5.0-T MRI and contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance angiography (CE-MRA). Twenty children with JIA and 10 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent hand 5.0-T MRI, including contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging and CE-MRA. The maximum synovial thickness, enhancement rate, bone marrow edema score, palmar digital artery diameter ratios, palmar arch integrity, distal microcirculation score, and vascular tortuosity were quantified. Correlations with the Juvenile Arthritis Disease Activity Score-27 (JADAS-27), erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR), and C-reactive protein (CRP) were analyzed. Compared with controls, the JIA group showed higher maximum synovial thickness (5.19±2.35 mm vs. 0.83±0.24 mm, P<0.001), enhancement rate (0.44±0.20 vs. 0.20±0.14, P=0.002), bone marrow edema score (median 7.50 vs. 0, P<0.001), and vascular tortuosity (2.0 vs. 0, P<0.001), but lower common palmar digital artery diameter ratio (0.690 vs. 1.000, P<0.001) and microcirculation score (1.0 vs. 3.0, P<0.001). The bone marrow edema score (r=0.674, P=0.001), maximum synovial thickness (r=0.581, P=0.007), and enhancement rate (r=0.634, P=0.003) correlated positively with JADAS-27, and the bone marrow edema score was independently associated with ln(JADAS-27) (standardized β=0.677, P=0.005). Combined 5.0-T MRI and CE-MRA revealed a distinct pattern of synovial inflammation, arterial narrowing, and impaired distal microcirculatory perfusion in children with JIA. CE-MRA-derived vascular parameters are candidate exploratory imaging markers requiring validation in larger multicenter cohorts.

items.title: Systematic review and meta-analysis on comparing treatment approaches of cervical fractures in ankylosing spondylitis to determine improvement in outcomes.
items.abstract: Anterior, posterior and combine surgical approach for treatment of cervical fractures in ankylosing spondylitis is debatable in current existing literature. There are recognized advantages and disadvantages associated with anterior, posterior, and combined surgical approaches to the cervical spine when treating fractures in patients with ankylosing spondylitis (AS). Despite growing surgical experience, the optimal approach with respect to neurological recovery, complication rates, and mortality remains unclear, and the choice is largely guided by surgeon expertise and patient-specific factors rather than high-quality comparative evidence. The study aimed to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis comparing treatment options for cervical fractures in patients with AS. The focus was on evaluating surgical approaches, complication rates, neurological outcomes. Systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted using specific keywords and related MeSH on PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, ClinicalTrials.gov to retrieve relevant literature. Only peer-reviewed English language original articles with full-text availability from 1st January, 1970 to 31st December, 2025 were considered. The pooled data analysis was conducted for binary outcomes through estimating odds ratios at 95% confidence interval with use of Mantel-Haenszel test. Forest plots were also generated for comparison of outcomes. Heterogeneity was assessed using (I²) using random effect model (I² > 50%) and fixed effect model (I² < 50%). The dichotomous model in meta-analysis was used to generate forest plots to assess heterogeneity. Funnel plots were also generated to determine the publication bias. In case of asymmetry in funnel plots, Rank correlation, Egger's regression test was performed to confirm the publication bias (p < 0.05). The statistical analysis was conducted on open meta-analyst Excel Binary Workbook. Eighteen retrospective studies encompassing 1441 patients (1275 male, 166 female; mean age range 40-72.7 years) met inclusion criteria. Mean CMS was 37.89 ± 5.71 (range 30-49), indicating uniformly poor methodological quality across all included studies. Across all nine pairwise comparisons, the only statistically significant finding was a higher complication rate with the anterior approach compared to the posterior approach (OR 2.97, 95% CI 1.23-7.19, p = 0.015; I² = 65.9%). Neurological recovery did not differ significantly in any pairwise comparison: combined vs. anterior (OR 0.97, 95% CI 0.41-2.29, p = 0.941; I² = 91.9%), combined vs. posterior (OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.32-1.26, p = 0.195; I² = 89.7%), and anterior vs. posterior (OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.45-1.07, p = 0.096; I² = 0.0%). Complication rates comparing combined vs. anterior (OR 0.90, 95% CI 0.49-1.68, p = 0.752) and combined vs. posterior (OR 1.48, 95% CI 0.98-2.25, p = 0.065) were not significantly different, though the latter demonstrated a marginal trend favoring the posterior approach. Mortality did not differ significantly across any comparison: combined vs. anterior (OR 1.99, 95% CI 0.84-4.72, p = 0.120; I² = 0%), combined vs. posterior (OR 1.43, 95% CI 0.77-2.63, p = 0.254; I² = 0%), and anterior vs. posterior (OR 1.20, 95% CI 0.17-8.49, p = 0.853; I² = 68.2%). Funnel plots and associated statistical tests indicated no evidence of small-study or publication bias across all comparisons (all Egger's and Kendall's p > 0.05). However, these findings should be regarded as low-certainty evidence given the exclusively retrospective study designs, uniformly poor CMS scores, and very high between-study heterogeneity in neurological recovery comparisons. Funnel plot symmetry and statistical tests (Egger's regression and Kendall's rank correlation, p > 0.05) indicated no evidence of small-study or publication bias across comparisons. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized the best currently available - though uniformly low-certainty - evidence on surgical approaches for ankylosing spondylitis-associated cervical fractures. Based on low-certainty retrospective evidence, the anterior approach is associated with a statistically significantly higher complication rate than the posterior approach, representing the only significant finding across nine pairwise comparisons. Neurological recovery and mortality were comparable across all three approach pairs. The posterior approach appears favorable from a complication-minimization perspective, particularly in patients with significant cardiopulmonary comorbidity, but this recommendation is based on low-certainty evidence and should not override individualized surgical decision-making based on fracture morphology, baseline neurological status, and surgeon expertise. Prospective, multicenter studies with standardized outcome reporting are required to generate higher-certainty evidence.

items.title: Staphylococcus aureus Purulent Myopericarditis and Cardiac Tamponade in a Patient With Systemic Lupus Erythematosus.
items.abstract: Purulent bacterial pericarditis (or myopericarditis) is a rare condition that can lead to the development of pericardial effusion and cardiac tamponade. We report a complicated case of methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus myopericarditis complicated by cardiac tamponade in a young, immunocompromised patient undergoing treatment for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This case highlights how SLE and immunosuppression can predispose patients to rare, life-threatening infections such as purulent myopericarditis. We review potential mechanisms of how bacterial pathogens may seed the pericardial space, as well as different treatment options that should be considered, including intravenous and, in some cases, intrapericardial antibiotic delivery. Purulent pericardial effusions can rapidly develop and progress to cardiac tamponade, hemodynamic instability, and death if not recognized promptly. SLE and immunosuppression are risk factors for the development of this rare condition.

items.title: Predictive and mechanistic evaluation of ODE-informed machine learning for systemic lupus erythematosus disease-activity stratification.
items.abstract: Mechanistic consistency does not necessarily imply improved prediction. We evaluated ordinary differential equation (ODE)-informed machine learning for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) disease-activity stratification, assessing predictive utility and mechanistic consistency separately. GSE65391 data classified 131 patients as high (n = 56) or low (n = 75) disease activity. A published four-state ODE generated anti-inflammatory, immune-complex, tissue-damage, and pro-inflammatory features. Architecture-matched Random Forest (RF) models were compared using feature ablation and outer-fold evaluation. Directionality, perturbation, and parameter sensitivity assessed mechanistic consistency; two independent SLE datasets supported exploratory proxy comparisons. RF + ODE initially achieved AUROC 0.7133 versus 0.5940 for RF alone (ΔAUROC=+0.1193; 95% CI, 0.0209-0.2140). Removing the outcome-coupled ODE residual reduced AUROC to 0.6708. Archived out-of-fold evaluation and independent outer-fold reimplementation yielded AUROCs of 0.6019 and 0.6529, respectively; neither established robust incremental discrimination. The reimplementation excluded held-out outcomes from predictor generation. Within the calibrated representation, anti-inflammatory, immune-complex, and pro-inflammatory states showed consistent disease-activity directionality, with strong immune-complex-pro-inflammatory coupling (Spearman ρ=0.912). Perturbation and parameter-sensitivity analyses supported stability of selected relationships. External modality-specific proxies showed exploratory directional analogy without validating source-defined states. The apparent predictive advantage attenuated under stricter evaluation, while selected state relationships remained stable under tested perturbations and parameter variation. The published ODE provided a structured representation for examining dynamical relationships, with incremental predictive value assessed separately. Mechanistic consistency and predictive utility should be evaluated as distinct dimensions.

items.title: Factors associated with structural progression of the sacroiliac joints on MRI in axial spondyloarthritis: a retrospective longitudinal study.
items.abstract: To identify clinical and routine sacroiliac joint (SIJ) MRI variables associated with structural damage progression in axial spondyloarthritis (axSpA). This retrospective longitudinal study enrolled 234 patients with axSpA who underwent at least two SIJ MRI examinations between August 2011 and March 2024 (643 examinations, 409 consecutive visit pairs). Progression at each follow-up examination relative to the previous one was adjudicated using an SSS-based three-step algorithm. Mixed-effects logistic regression with patient-specific random intercepts identified factors associated with progression, with the MRI follow-up interval as a covariate. Multicollinearity was assessed using variance inflation factors, and treatment exposure was evaluated in a sensitivity analysis. Progression was identified in 260 of 409 follow-up examinations (63.6%). After adjustment for the MRI follow-up interval, a higher erosion SSS score (odds ratio [OR] 1.178, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.099-1.262, P < 0.001), smoking (OR 2.023, 95% CI 1.091-3.751, P = 0.025), and HLA-B27 positivity (OR 2.929, 95% CI 1.225-7.007, P = 0.016) were independently associated with increased progression risk, whereas older age at diagnosis (OR 0.970, 95% CI 0.946-0.993, P = 0.012) was associated with decreased risk; these associations were essentially unchanged after forced entry of treatment exposure. A higher erosion burden at the previous examination, smoking, and HLA-B27 positivity were associated with SIJ structural damage progression; patients diagnosed at a younger age also warrant attention. Given the retrospective observational design, these are statistical associations whose causality and clinical utility require prospective validation.

items.title: Genetically proxied sex hormones, Sjögren's disease, and broad dry eye disease: A bidirectional two-sample mendelian randomization study.
items.abstract: ObjectiveTo evaluate bidirectional associations of genetically proxied total testosterone and estradiol with Sjögren's disease (SjD) and broad dry eye disease (DED) using female-derived, male-derived, and sex-combined hormone GWASs.MethodsWe conducted bidirectional two-sample Mendelian randomization using European-ancestry genome-wide association studies (GWASs). Forward analyses evaluated total-testosterone and estradiol traits from female-derived, male-derived, and sex-combined GWASs against FinnGen SjD (3,309 cases and 484,260 controls) and Million Veteran Program broad DED (84,262 cases and 314,374 controls); reverse analyses used disease instruments to estimate disease-to-hormone associations. Primary instruments met P < 5 × 10 -8 and F > 10. Secondary forward SjD analyses used bioavailable-testosterone and testosterone-cluster instruments. Inverse-variance-weighted (IVW) estimates were complemented by weighted median, pleiotropy diagnostics, major histocompatibility complex (MHC) exclusion, Steiger orientation, and direction-specific LDtrait analyses.ResultsSex-combined total testosterone was inverse for SjD by IVW (26 variants; odds ratio [OR], 0.41; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.23-0.72; P = 0.002) and weighted median (OR, 0.30; 95% CI, 0.14-0.68; P = 0.004). The IVW estimate remained inverse after LDtrait exclusion. Male- and female-derived total-testosterone estimates were null and directionally discordant. Sex-combined bioavailable testosterone was also inverse (73 variants; OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.33-0.76; P = 0.001); the other four secondary IVW estimates did not meet correction, and all five secondary sets were heterogeneous. No estradiol-SjD, hormone-DED, or reverse IVW estimate met correction. Reverse sensitivity signals were not robust to MHC exclusion.ConclusionsSex-combined total- and bioavailable-testosterone estimates were concordantly inverse for SjD, but sex-specific estimates were null. The data establish neither a common effect across sex strata, independence from sex hormone-binding globulin, nor a disease-to-hormone association. Sparse estradiol and reverse instruments constrain inference. Larger sex-stratified SjD datasets are needed; these findings do not support hormone testing or treatment.

items.title: Sjögren's Syndrome-Associated Medium- and Large-Vessel Vasculitis Presenting With Acute Abdominal Symptoms.
items.abstract: We report a case of Sjögren's syndrome-associated vasculitis involving the medium and large arteries in a patient who presented with acute abdominal pain, vomiting, and fever. Computed tomography angiography demonstrated vasculitic involvement of the superior mesenteric, inferior mesenteric, renal, and left external iliac arteries. Immunological evaluation revealed strongly positive antinuclear antibodies (ANA) and an extractable nuclear antigen (ENA) profile positive for anti-SSA, anti-SSB, and Ro-52 antibodies, while anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibodies were negative. The patient responded rapidly to systemic corticosteroid therapy and was discharged on oral treatment. This case highlights a rare presentation of Sjögren's syndrome with medium- and large-vessel vasculitis manifesting as acute abdominal symptoms.

items.title: Fulminant Seronegative Systemic Lupus Erythematosus With Class IV/V Lupus Nephritis and Multisystem Involvement.
items.abstract: Seronegative systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) poses a diagnostic challenge, particularly when patients develop organ-threatening disease despite negative traditional serologies. We report a fulminant case in a 24-year-old woman with congenital atrioventricular (AV) block, chronic pancytopenia, chronic kidney disease (CKD), and morbid obesity, who presented with progressive anasarca, dyspnea, dizziness, and cough. Laboratory evaluation revealed severe pancytopenia, nephrotic-range proteinuria 11-13 g/day (reference range: 0-150 mg/24 hours), and acute kidney injury. Renal biopsy demonstrated Class IV proliferative and Class V membranous lupus nephritis, despite negative antinuclear antibodies (ANA), anti-double-stranded DNA (anti-dsDNA) antibodies, anti-Smith (anti-Sm) antibodies, anti-Sjögren's-syndrome-related antigen A (SSA) and antigen B (SSB) antibodies, and normal complement levels. Within 24 hours, she developed hypoxia, hemoglobin drop, and a right subcapsular renal hematoma. Echocardiography revealed dilated cardiomyopathy, severe aortic insufficiency with valvular vegetation, and suspected pacing-induced cardiomyopathy, progressing to cardiogenic shock requiring inotropes. She developed necrotizing mucocutaneous lesions, vasculitic purpura, pseudomembranous colitis secondary to Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile), and microangiopathic hemolysis. Despite high-dose steroids and mycophenolate, her condition deteriorated, necessitating transfer for plasmapheresis and rituximab. Seronegative SLE represents up to 5% of cases and is often associated with severe, multisystem involvement. Seronegativity may reflect low antibody titers, immune complex sequestration, or assay variability. This case underscores that negative serologies do not exclude SLE, and early recognition through clinical suspicion and tissue biopsy is critical. Aggressive immunosuppression and multidisciplinary care are essential in managing fulminant seronegative lupus with severe nephritis, vasculopathy, and systemic complications.

items.title: Targeted intestinal ROS scavenging alleviated rheumatoid arthritis by microbial metabolite kynurenic acid mediated Treg/Th17 balance through AhR pathway activation.
items.abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune disorder characterized by immune dysregulation, which is often closely related to impaired gut microbiota homeostasis. Excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) are recognized as critical drivers of microecological immunity disturbance, contributing directly to the inflammatory cascade. However, the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Here, we have used ROS scavengers to alleviate RA progression via inhibiting intestinal ROS and modulating gut microbial kynurenic acid metabolism. Black phosphorus nanosheets (BPNSs), as effective ROS scavengers, significantly ameliorated disease severity in collagen-induced arthritis (CIA) mice by oral administration to eliminate intestinal excess ROS. BPNSs selectively reshaped the gut microbiota and altered its metabolic profile, elevating the relative abundance of the tryptophan-derived metabolite kynurenic acid (KYNA). Mechanistically, elevated KYNA activated the aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) pathway in naïve CD4 + T cells, promoting their differentiation into Treg cells through the inhibition of AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. The therapeutic effect of KYNA was further corroborated in CIA mice, where its administration maintained Treg/Th17 balance, attenuated arthritis progression, and enhanced intestinal barrier integrity. These findings elucidate novel gut-immune-bone axis wherein scavenging intestinal ROS drives KYNA mediated AhR-dependent Treg cell differentiation, thereby proposing a promising ROS scavenging-based strategy for RA treatment.

items.title: Treatment persistence and clinical outcomes following subcutaneous methotrexate initiation in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a real-world observational study.
items.abstract: This study aimed to evaluate treatment persistence and safety following subcutaneous methotrexate (MTX) initiation in Japanese patients with RA and to assess clinical outcomes among patients who directly switched from oral to subcutaneous MTX. This retrospective study included 101 patients with RA who initiated subcutaneous MTX at our institution. Efficacy and safety were analysed in patients who switched from oral MTX due to adverse events. The primary endpoint was the 26-week retention rate of subcutaneous MTX. Gastrointestinal intolerance was the commonest reason for switching from oral to subcutaneous MTX. The overall retention rate was 87.1% (88/101). Among 88 patients who switched, the 26-week retention rate was 92.0% (81/88). During 26 weeks after switching, MTX dose increased in 46.6% (41/88). In patients not receiving biologic or targeted synthetic disease-modifying anti-rheumatic drugs at switching (n=50), the 26-week retention rate was 96.0% (48/50), and mean MTX dose increased (10.3±2.8 to 12.0±2.8 mg/week; p<0.0001). The Clinical Disease Activity Index improved by week 26 (13.2±10.1 to 8.2±7.8; p<0.0001), with 30.0% (15/50) achieving remission. Switching from oral to subcutaneous MTX in patients with RA who are intolerant to oral MTX may enable continued treatment and dose optimization and be associated with improved disease activity.

items.title: Association between ankylosing spondylitis and hearing loss: A Mendelian randomization study.
items.abstract: Observational studies have suggested a potential link between ankylosing spondylitis (AS) and hearing loss. However, this association remains controversial due to potential drug-induced ototoxicity from treatments. Therefore, we employed a Mendelian randomization (MR) approach to evaluate the association between AS and hearing loss from a genetic perspective. This MR study utilized summary data from genome-wide association studies on AS and hearing loss, including sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL) and conductive hearing loss (CHL). The primary analysis was conducted using the inverse-variance weighted method. The primary analysis showed a causal effect of AS on both SNHL (odds ratio [OR] = 1.121, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.042-1.206, P = .002) and CHL (OR = 1.387, 95% CI: 1.123-1.712, P = .002). After excluding chromosome 6 variants, the association with CHL persisted (OR = 1.675, 95% CI: 1.212-2.315, P = .002), while the effect on SNHL was no longer significant (OR = 1.054, 95% CI: 0.942-1.181, P = .357). The primary inverse-variance weighted analysis showed no causal effect of SNHL on AS (OR = 0.984, 95% CI: 0.892-1.086, P = .747). Sensitivity analyses found no evidence of horizontal pleiotropy. This MR study suggests that AS is causally associated with higher risks of CHL and SNHL. The association with CHL appears independent of the chromosome 6 human leukocyte antigen region, whereas the risk for SNHL is largely driven by this region. These findings suggest that targeted audiometric evaluations should be considered for symptomatic patients with AS. Further studies are required to explore the specific mechanisms linking AS to different types of hearing loss.

items.title: Comparison analysis of the triglyceride-glucose index, triglyceride-glucose and frailty index in cardiovascular disease and mortality association among patients with rheumatoid arthritis: A population-based cohort study.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is a major cause of excess mortality among patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Conventional risk assessment may not fully capture the metabolic abnormalities and physiological vulnerability associated with RA. We investigated whether the triglyceride-glucose-frailty index (TyG-FI), which combines a surrogate marker of insulin resistance with accumulated health deficits, was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among adults with RA. We analyzed 1090 adults with self-reported RA from 10 cycles of the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey conducted between 1999 and 2018. TyG-FI was calculated as the product of the triglyceride-glucose index and a 49-item deficit-accumulation frailty index. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the association with prevalent CVD, whereas Cox proportional hazards regression was used to examine cardiovascular mortality. Restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses, sensitivity analyses, and discrimination analyses were conducted as secondary analyses. In the fully adjusted models, each 1-unit higher TyG-FI was associated with higher odds of prevalent CVD (odds ratio, 4.50; 95% confidence interval, 3.20-6.33) and a higher hazard of cardiovascular mortality (hazard ratio, 1.77; 95% confidence interval, 1.16-2.70). The reported areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve were 0.80 for prevalent CVD and 0.81 for cardiovascular mortality in models incorporating TyG-FI, compared with 0.73 and 0.80, respectively, in models incorporating TyG. An exploratory subgroup analysis suggested a stronger association between TyG-FI and prevalent CVD among participants aged ≤65 years (P for interaction = .044). Higher TyG-FI was associated with prevalent CVD and cardiovascular mortality among US adults with self-reported RA. TyG-FI may capture complementary metabolic and frailty-related information; however, its incremental predictive value, calibration, clinical utility, and external validity require further evaluation before clinical implementation.

items.title: Association of the dietary carbohydrate-to-fiber ratio with prevalent rheumatoid arthritis in NHANES 2009-2018.
items.abstract: This study examines the cross-sectional association between the carbohydrate-to-fiber ratio (CFR), an indicator of carbohydrate quality, and prevalent rheumatoid arthritis (RA) in the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES). The exposure was overall CFR, calculated from 2 days of dietary recall and categorized into population-wide quartiles. RA diagnosis was the outcome. Survey-weighted logistic regression was used to evaluate the CFR-RA association, adjusting for demographic, lifestyle, dietary, and metabolic covariates. Generalized additive models, subgroup analyses, and interaction tests were performed. An exploratory survey-weighted mediation analysis evaluated SII as a hypothesized intermediate factor. The study ultimately included 19,260 participants aged ≥ 20 years with valid 2-day dietary weights, with a survey-weighted RA prevalence of 4.31%. Higher CFR was significantly associated with increased RA odds, with the highest quartile showing 67% higher odds than the lowest (P < .001). After exclusion of CFR values above the upper fence defined using the interquartile range, the model 4 GAM showed an effectively linear positive association. A sensitivity analysis retaining all CFR observations showed curvature in the sparsely populated upper tail with wide uncertainty. In the exploratory model 4 mediation analysis, the estimated indirect association through SII was small (4.77% of the total association; 95% confidence interval: -5.33% to 14.87%), and its confidence interval included the null. Higher CFR was associated with greater odds of prevalent self-reported RA. Longitudinal and genetically informed studies are needed before causal or preventive interpretations can be made.

items.title: Association of baseline non-severe anemia with clinical outcomes following the first recorded diagnosis of systemic sclerosis: A matched cohort study.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) carries the highest mortality among systemic autoimmune diseases, yet the prognostic significance of anemia around the time of the first recorded SSc diagnosis is unclear. We examined whether baseline anemia is associated with early mortality and complications. This retrospective matched cohort study identified female adults with a first recorded SSc diagnosis between January 2010 and December 2024 from the TriNetX Research Network. Patients were required to have at least 5 years of pre-index observation without a documented SSc diagnosis. The network comprised 140 healthcare organizations, with approximately 70% of patients in the United States across all 9 census regions and 30% at international sites. Anemia was defined as hemoglobin (Hb) ≥8.0 and <12.0 g/dL and non-anemia as ≥12.0 g/dL, measured within ±30 days of diagnosis. For the Hb-stratified analysis, the anemia cohort was categorized as Hb ≥10.0 to <12.0 g/dL or ≥8.0 to <10.0 g/dL. One-to-one propensity score matching balanced baseline characteristics, and Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). The primary outcome was all-cause mortality during days 31 to 365 among patients surviving the 30-day landmark period; secondary outcomes were sepsis, acute kidney injury, intensive care unit admission, pulmonary fibrosis, and elevated C-reactive protein (≥10 mg/L). After matching, 5410 patients remained in each cohort. Baseline anemia was significantly associated with higher 1-year mortality (HR, 2.54; 95% CI, 1.99-3.22; P < .001) and with increased risks of sepsis (HR, 3.20; 95% CI, 2.38-4.30), acute kidney injury (HR, 2.24; 95% CI, 1.80-2.78), intensive care unit admission (HR, 1.92; 95% CI, 1.47-2.51), and elevated C-reactive protein (HR, 1.55; 95% CI, 1.37-1.74; all P < .001); no significant association was observed for pulmonary fibrosis (HR, 1.06; 95% CI, 0.96-1.17; P = .229). Associations persisted in sensitivity analyses and over 3-year follow-up. Mortality risk showed a graded pattern across Hb strata (Hb ≥10.0-<12.0 g/dL: HR, 1.66; Hb ≥8.0-<10.0 g/dL: HR, 3.33). Baseline anemia was associated with increased mortality and acute systemic complications following the first recorded SSc diagnosis; these observational findings warrant prospective validation.

items.title: Sarcopenia in systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease: A cross-sectional radiological and functional assessment.
items.abstract: Systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease (SSc-ILD) is a significant complication that impairs lung function and increases morbidity. Sarcopenia, characterized by the loss of muscle mass and function, is commonly found in chronic diseases such as systemic sclerosis. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of sarcopenia in patients with SSc-ILD and investigate its cross-sectional associations with pulmonary function test parameters, estimated pulmonary artery pressure and quantitative radiological lung involvement. In this cross-sectional study conducted between 2024 and 2025, 40 patients with systemic sclerosis (2013 ACR/EULAR criteria) and high-resolution computed tomography-confirmed interstitial lung disease were evaluated. Patients with overlap myositis, acute infections, severe orthopedic/neurological limitations, and end-stage organ failure were excluded. Sarcopenia was diagnosed based on European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People 2 criteria using muscle mass (bioelectrical impedance analysis) and handgrip strength measurements. Pulmonary function tests (FVC, single-breath transfer factor of lung for carbon monoxide), echocardiographic sPAP estimations, and quantitative high-resolution computed tomography lung density analysis were performed. These findings highlight the potential impact of sarcopenia on lung function and the association of sarcopenia with radiological findings in SSc-ILD SSc-ILD. Among the 40 analyzed patients (mean age: 55.8 ± 10.8 years, 85.0% female, mean BMI: 28.7 ± 5.0 kg/m2), sarcopenia was identified in 10 patients (25.0%). Patients with and without sarcopenia were compared to analyze its effects on pulmonary function and radiological findings. Patients with sarcopenia had significantly lower lung diffusion capacity (transfer factor of lung for carbon monoxide) and forced vital capacity % values and significantly higher radiological lung involvement compared to those without sarcopenia (P = .004, P = .023, and P = .035, respectively). Systolic pulmonary artery pressure was also significantly higher in sarcopenic patients (P = .031). Additionally, fat-free mass index, fat-free mass, muscle mass, and handgrip strength were significantly lower in sarcopenic patients (P < .001).

items.title: Adult-onset Still Disease Flare 5 Days Following Poly-l-lactic Acid Injection: A Cautionary Tale for Aesthetic Practice.
items.abstract: Adult-onset Still disease (AOSD) is a rare systemic autoinflammatory disorder characterized by quotidian fevers, evanescent rash, and polyarthritis. Minimally invasive aesthetic procedures are increasingly common, yet their immunological safety in patients with underlying autoimmune disease remains poorly characterized. We report a 57-year-old woman with AOSD, previously stable on annual rituximab (1 g), who developed a severe systemic flare temporally associated with a poly-l-lactic acid facial injection, with symptom onset 5 days after the procedure. She presented with high-grade pyrexia (40°C), extreme leukocytosis (white blood cell, 26 × 10 9 /L), C-reactive protein (230 mg/L), and acute arthritis of the hand joints, requiring inpatient intravenous corticosteroids and intravenous rituximab. This case raises the possibility that collagen-stimulating biomaterials may act as an immunological trigger for systemic autoinflammatory relapse in predisposed patients; however, causality cannot be inferred from a single observation, and the relationship described here is strictly temporal. As a conceptual, hypothesis-generating proposal, a structured preprocedural risk assessment and multidisciplinary perioperative protocol are suggested for consideration before elective aesthetic procedures in AOSD patients, pending validation in larger series.

items.title: Sexual Dysfunction and Associated Factors in Iranian Women with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus: A Cross-Sectional Study.
items.abstract: Sexual dysfunction is a prevalent yet under-investigated dimension of quality of life in women with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). This study aimed to determine the prevalence of sexual dysfunction and its associated demographic, reproductive, and SLE-related clinical factors among Iranian women with SLE. This cross-sectional study enrolled women with SLE recruited from private rheumatology practices in two Iranian cities between December 2025 and June 2026. Data were collected via a clinical-demographic questionnaire and the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI). Of 116 recruited women, 97 participants were included in the final analysis. Univariable and multivariable (backward elimination) linear regression models were used to identify factors associated with total and subdomain FSFI scores. The mean (±SD) age of participants was 39.31 (±8.11) years, and sexual dysfunction was identified in 68 of 97 women (70.1%). Arousal 2.65 (±0.59) and desire 3.02 (±1.16) were the most impaired domains, while pain 5.06 (±1.08) was the least affected. In multivariable analysis, active lupus showed the strongest association with poorer sexual function, with significantly lower total FSFI scores (β=-5.33; 95% CI: -6.83, -3.82; P<0.001) and all subdomains (P≤0.009). Longer disease duration and older age at SLE diagnosis were independently associated with lower total, arousal, and satisfaction scores. Current infertility in a small subgroup (n=11/97), higher intercourse frequency, and unemployment were associated with better sexual outcomes in specific domains, while higher parity and chronic comorbidities were associated with worse orgasm and pain scores, respectively. Sexual dysfunction is highly prevalent among Iranian women with SLE, particularly affecting arousal and desire. Disease activity, duration, and age at diagnosis are independently associated factors. These findings suggest the potential value of integrating routine sexual health assessments into comprehensive SLE care.

items.title: Feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining therapeutic electrical stimulation using belt electrodes and nutritional management in patients with rheumatoid arthritis: a pilot study.
items.abstract: Although resistance training with nutritional intervention is recommended for sarcopenia, effective programs are often difficult to implement in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA). This pilot study aimed to assess the feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining therapeutic electrical stimulation (TES) using belt electrodes with nutritional management in patients with RA. This pilot study was conducted as a prospective observational study with a single-arm before-after framework and enrolled outpatients with RA in remission or with low disease activity. Participants received an outpatient rehabilitation program as part of routine clinical practice once or twice weekly over 6 months, including TES applied to the lower limbs using belt electrodes (20 min per session; 20 Hz; maximum tolerable intensity) and the daily intake of an L-leucine-enriched protein-containing nutritional supplement. Feasibility and safety were evaluated based on study completion, TES session frequency, verbally confirmed adherence to nutritional supplementation, adverse events documented during the program, and maintenance of disease activity. Lower-limb lean mass, knee extensor muscle strength, and gait speed were assessed as exploratory clinical outcomes at baseline and after 6 months. Of the 14 recruited outpatients with RA, 10 completed both the 6-month program and the final outcome assessment, corresponding to a study completion rate of 71.4%. Participants received a median of 34.5 TES sessions over 6 months. As exploratory clinical outcomes, the median paired changes in lower-limb lean mass, knee extensor muscle strength, and gait speed were 0.08 kg (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.00 to 0.25; P  = 0.043), 1.58 kgf (95% CI, -0.35 to 7.25; P  = 0.084), and 0.18 m/s (95% CI, -0.04 to 0.24; P  = 0.084), respectively. Disease activity remained within the low disease activity to remission range and did not significantly change during the 6-month observation period ( P  = 0.214). No joint-related or cardiovascular adverse events were documented. This pilot study provides preliminary information on the feasibility and safety of a 6-month outpatient rehabilitation program combining TES using belt electrodes and nutritional management in patients with RA. These findings may inform the design of future studies.

items.title: Association of phenotypic and functional characteristics of regulatory T cells from minor salivary glands with expression of the delta 7 FoxP3 splice variant in patients with Sjögren's disease.
items.abstract: Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by lymphoplasmacytic infiltration of exocrine glands, including minor salivary glands (MSG), with potential formation of ectopic germinal centers. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are critical suppressors of autoimmune responses, and their dysfunction has been implicated in SjD pathogenesis. FoxP3, the master transcription factor of Tregs, undergoes alternative splicing to produce four variants: full-length (FL), Δ2, Δ7, and Δ2Δ7. While FoxP3 splice variants are known to influence Treg proliferation and suppressive activity, their profile and functional significance in Tregs from SjD patients remain poorly characterized. Peripheral blood was collected from 20 SjD patients or 20 healthy donors (HD). MSG biopsies were obtained from 10 SjD patients. Tregs were isolated from blood and biopsy tissue by immunomagnetic separation and expanded ex vivo. FoxP3 splice variant mRNA levels were quantified by real-time RT-PCR. Treg phenotype (CD4, CD25, CD127, CD152, Helios), suppressive molecules (CD39, CD223, granzymes A/B, perforin), was assessed by flow cytometry. The concentrations of suppressive cytokines IL-10 andIL-35 were accessed by Bio-Plex assay. Proliferation was evaluated by cell counting. Suppressive activity was determined by mixed lymphocyte reaction. Splice-switching oligonucleotides (SSOs) were used to induce Δ7 FoxP3 expression to confirm direct functional effects. Peripheral blood Tregs from SjD patients showed significantly decreased increased Δ7 FoxP3 splice variant compared to HD. MSG-derived Tregs from SjD patients also predominantly expressed the Δ7 FoxP3 variant. High-expressing Δ7 FoxP3 Tregs exhibited reduced proliferative activity, division frequency and decreased suppressive activity compared to low-expressing Δ7 FoxP3 Tregs. High-expressing Δ7 FoxP3 Tregs showed significantly reduced CD127low and Helios expression, decreased CD39, CD223, granzyme, and granzyme B. IL-10 and IL-35 production was also reduced. SSO-mediated induction of Δ7 FoxP3 MSG-derived Tregs confirmed these phenotypic and functional changes. This study demonstrates that elevated Δ7 FoxP3 splice variant expression in MSG-derived Tregs from SjD patients is associated with impaired proliferative and suppressive function, reduced expression of suppressive molecules and cytokines, and a phenotype suggestive of a transitional or immature Treg state. The results highlight the functional consequences of altered FoxP3 alternative splicing in SjD pathogenesis and suggest a possible involvement of Tregs in the biology of ectopic germinal centers in SjD.
